newsitem.title: JAPAN: Okinawa governor gives OK on U.S. bases - NHK.
newsitem.headline: Okinawa governor gives OK on U.S. bases - NHK.

text.p: Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota said on Friday he would take steps to renew land leases for U.S. military bases on Japan's southernmost island, NHK public broadcasting network reported.

It said Ota had made the "formal decision" and was expected hold a news conference shortly to announce his decision, which puts an end to a year-long bitter standoff with the central government in Tokyo.

Following the rape last year of an Okinawan schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen, a case that re-ignited protests against the presence of the U.S. military on the island, Ota refused to sign orders to renew leases for the bases.

Earlier this week, Ota won a promise from Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Okinawa would get special funds to improve the economy of the prefecture, the poorest in Japan with average income half that of Tokyo's.
The leases, held by some 3,000 landowners opposed to U.S. military bases, expire next May, which made Ota's stance a potential threat to U.S. use of the facilities.
